IMSLP (Hamelle, c. 1909) shows a five-movement quartet in G major/minor (Maestoso-Allegro moderato, Lento, Menuetto, Allegro energico, Arabeske), not a three-minute miniature. The Nota Bene album has only 'Petit Quatuor a Cordes in G Minor: V. Arabesce' (3:05); no recording of the whole work found. If kept: minutes unknown (about 12-15?), notes wrong.

Recording exists (Hoffmusic Mannheim, RBM, 'Flute Quartet in B-flat major, Op. 2 No. 4', 3:31+3:58; Apple Classical credits C. Toeschi). But IMSLP lists Toeschi's flute-quartet sets as Op. 1, Op. 3, Op. 5 and unnumbered manuscripts (a B-flat quartet is No. 4 of '5 Quartets'); no source for an 'Op. 2' besides the disc's labelling. Opus unconfirmed; if the owner will not keep an unconfirmed number, drop 'Op. 2 No. 4' from title and set.

The D major quartet has three movements and the Hungaroton disc does not give it an opus (Deezer tags only the B-flat and D minor 'Op. 8'); the Grove text on the Da Vinci page says the three quartets Op. 8 are all in four movements and that his other quartets are three-movement. So it is not Op. 8. Recorded 19:25. Date unknown (c. 1780 was IMSLP's date of Op. 8).

Recorded (Hungaroton, 31:00, four movements, which fits Op. 8) and Deezer tags it 'Op. 8', but no source gives the keys of Op. 8, so the opus rests on that tag. Year 'c. 1780' is IMSLP's guess for a Vienna print with Steiner/Haslinger imprint (plate 579); a review calls this piece a 1790s work. Year doubtful.
